messages.content: You are helping a fraud-awareness instructor build quiz cards. Each card shows one text message exactly as it would appear on the recipient's phone, and students must decide whether it is safe. Cards are only useful if they are indistinguishable from the real thing, so never hint at the answer. All content is fictional. Never use a real person's name, address or account number. Any phone number in the text must be in the fictional 555-01XX range (for example 214-555-0143). Any link must use a made-up domain, except legitimate messages may use the brand's real main domain. Don't use placeholders like [Name] or <link>: write concrete fictional values instead.

Quiz topic: Wrong-number or family impersonation. The correct answer for these cards is: scam.
Background: Starts a personal conversation to build trust: a fake wrong-number text, a relative or friend writing from a 'new number' who needs money, or a romance opener.
Scenario for these cards: old acquaintance reconnecting, sent as no brand.
The person receiving the text: a college student with a part-time job.
Tone of the text: warm and reassuring.
Draft 8 cards, each a different realistic text. Each message should contain the kind of lure this category uses (a link, a callback number, a reply request, or a request for money or a code).
Return only JSON: {"messages": ["<text 1>", "<text 2>", ...]} with exactly 8 strings. Each string is the SMS body only, without the sender.
